hero.tagline: An impressionist journey through light, philosophy & the cosmos

moon.label: I. The Moon
moon.heading: Selene's silver chariot
moon.intro: Ptolemy believed the Moon's influence caused tides, madness, and the cycles of life. While science has explained the tides, the Moon still governs the menstrual cycle, the migration of birds, and the spawning of coral — life itself dances to the Moon's rhythm.

philosophy.label: II. The Waves
philosophy.heading: Ego, arrogance & the ocean of self
philosophy.intro: The Bhagavad Gita warns: 'The ego is the greatest enemy of the human soul.' When Arjuna asks Krishna about the nature of the self, the answer is not 'I am great' but 'I am not the doer.'

gita.label: III. The Battlefield
gita.heading: Wisdom from the Bhagavad Gita
gita.intro: 'Whenever dharma declines and the purpose of life is forgotten, I manifest myself.' The Gita teaches that the divine does not abandon the world — it returns, again and again, to restore balance.

shiva.label: IV. The Dance
shiva.heading: Shiva & the cosmic rhythm
shiva.intro: Shiva is called Mahakala — the great time. He is not bound by time; he is time itself. Past, present, and future are all one in the dance of Mahakala.

art.label: V. The Canvas
art.heading: Art, beauty & the act of seeing
art.intro: The flute is the oldest instrument — a hollow reed that sings when breath passes through it. It teaches that music is not made but revealed, not created but discovered in the space between silence and sound.
